sources.entry: hitobito - Manage complex group hierarchies with members, events and a lot more. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Ruby

summary.one_liner: Hitobito is an open source Ruby web application for managing organisations and communities with complex group hierarchies, members, events, courses, and mailings.
summary.what_it_does: Hitobito is a web application for organisations and communities that need to manage members across nested group structures. The README describes it as covering members, events, courses, mailings, and communication. Groups are always of a specific type and arranged in a tree, and each group type can define its own role types with permissions. The core does not ship with any group or role types; these must be defined in a separate plugin (called a wagon) tailored to the organisation. Documentation covers development, deployment, interfaces, API, OAuth and OIDC, and a generic user guide is available in German. The README names Wagons as the plugin framework and references a development kit and rake tasks for wagons.
use_cases: manage members of an organisation with nested groups
run events and courses for a community
define custom group and role types for an association
provide OAuth or OIDC login for member data
how_to_run: Read the development documentation in doc/developer for setup and deployment instructions
Use the development kit referenced in the README
Create or install a wagon that defines your group types, since the core ships with none
notable: Meta-model for group hierarchies: groups are typed, arranged in a tree, and each type defines role types with permissions
Plugin architecture based on Wagons; a wagon is required to define group types
Permissions are derived from the roles a user holds in different groups
Documentation includes API, OAuth and OIDC interfaces
Used by many Swiss organisations, per the README community list
caveats: Core has no built-in group or role types; a separate wagon is required before it is usable
Main user guide is in German, and architecture docs are in German
Deployment and setup details are in separate documentation rather than the README
